title: Finite-height bounds and compatible rank-one coarsenings
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension], let $W\subseteq L$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], and put $R=W\cap K$. Suppose $R$ has finite height $h$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=d<\infty$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Height counts strict inclusions in chains of prime ideals. Then $W$ has finite height at most $h+d$. For any overring $W\subseteq A\subseteq L$, $A$ is a valuation ring, $\mathfrak m_A\subseteq W$, $W/\mathfrak m_A$ is a valuation ring of $A/\mathfrak m_A$, and $W$ is its inverse image under $A\to A/\mathfrak m_A$. Heights add under this composition. If $h>0$ and $(R\setminus\{0\})^{-1}W=L$, then there is an overring $A\subset L$ of height one whose restriction $A\cap K=R_1$ has height one. Put $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap K=\mathfrak m_{R_1}$. Then $R_0=R/\mathfrak p$ is a valuation ring of $k=R_1/\mathfrak p$ of height $h-1$, $W_0=W/\mathfrak q$ is a valuation ring of $E=A/\mathfrak q$, and $W_0\cap k=R_0$. The coarsened valuations on $K,L$ are compatible. For a subfield $F\subseteq L$ containing $K$, restriction to $F$ commutes with these inverse-image descriptions.
